title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
prompt: You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. In one operation, you can choose an index of `nums` and increment the element at that index by `1`. Return the maximum possible frequency of an element after performing at most `k` operations. You may perform the operation on the same index multiple times.

examples.explanation: Increment nums[0] three times and nums[1] two times to make nums = [4,4,4]. All three elements now equal 4, using exactly 5 operations.
There are multiple ways to achieve a frequency of 2, e.g. turning [1,4] into [4,4], or [4,8] into [8,8], or [8,13] into [13,13].

hints: Sort the array first: once sorted, making a group of elements equal always means raising all of them up to the value of the rightmost (largest) element in that group.

For a sorted window [left, right], the cost to make every element equal to nums[right] is nums[right] * windowSize - sum(window). Use a sliding window and a running sum to evaluate this in O(1) per step.

Expand right; whenever the cost exceeds k, shrink from the left (removing it from the running sum) until the cost is within budget again. Track the max window size seen — it represents the largest achievable frequency.

solution.approach: Sort the array so that any window of elements can only be made equal by raising every element up to the window's maximum (its rightmost element). For a window [left, right], the total operations needed is nums[right] * (right - left + 1) - sum(window). Slide a window with a running sum: expand right each step, and while the cost exceeds k, shrink from the left, removing the leaving element from the running sum. The window size is always a valid achievable frequency, so track the maximum size reached.
solution.code:
def max_frequency(nums, k):
    nums.sort()
    left = 0
    window_sum = 0
    best = 1

    for right in range(len(nums)):
        window_sum += nums[right]
        while nums[right] * (right - left + 1) - window_sum > k:
            window_sum -= nums[left]
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)

    return best
